Definition: a primary inseparable particle of uncertain derivation; used only in composition as a prefix; hard, i.e. with difficulty:--+ hard, + grievous, etc.
BiblicalUsage: Hard, ill, difficult, the inseparable prefix that turns a good word bad, as in hard to bear or hard to understand. It never stands on its own in the Greek New Testament; it only ever appears joined to another word, doing its work inside it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the little prefix preaches its own sermon: some things are hard by nature, and the gospel never pretends otherwise.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
